context.title: Finite-field list conjecture for matroid representability
context.statement: Let $k$ be a prime power. The claim concerns matroids and representability over fields and finite fields $\operatorname{GF}(q)$. **Finite-field list conjecture.** There exists a number $n_k$ such that, for all matroids $M$, $M$ is representable over all fields with at least $k$ elements if and only if it is representable over all finite fields $\operatorname{GF}(q)$ with $k \leq q \leq n_k$. This generalizes the characterization of near-regular matroids; the paper states that the conjecture remains open, including for $k=4$.
context.source_name: R. A. Pendavingh and S. H. M. van Zwam, “Lifts of matroid representations over partial fields”, arXiv:0804.3263 (2009).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.3263

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2008).

context.title: Chartrand's existence conjecture for prescribed rainbow connection numbers
context.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $rc(G)$ and $src(G)$ denote its rainbow connection number and strong rainbow connection number, respectively. Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers. **Chartrand's conjecture.** There exists a connected graph $G$ such that $rc(G)=a$ and $src(G)=b$ if and only if $a=b\in\{1,2\}$ or $3\leq a\leq b$. The conjecture asks whether the lower bound on $b$ in the preceding existence theorem can be removed; it was subsequently confirmed by Chen and Li, who constructed graphs with the prescribed parameters.
context.source_name: Xueliang Li and Yuefang Sun, “Rainbow connections of graphs – A survey”, arXiv:1101.5747 (2011).
context.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2011). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1012.2693](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.2693).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.5747

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2011); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

context.title: The $\mathbb{P}_4$ characterization conjecture for matroid representability
context.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be an indeterminate, and define the partial field

$$
\mathbb{P}_4:= \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{Q}(\alpha),\{\alpha,\alpha-1,\alpha+1,\alpha-2\}).
$$

**$\mathbb{P}_4$ characterization conjecture.** A matroid $M$ is representable over all finite fields with at least $4$ elements if and only if $M$ is representable over $\mathbb{P}_4$. The statement is offered as a candidate after the preceding finite-field list conjecture could not be proved even for $k=4$; no resolution is given.
context.source_name: R. A. Pendavingh and S. H. M. van Zwam, “Lifts of matroid representations over partial fields”, arXiv:0804.3263 (2009).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.3263

context.title: Positive-coefficient conjecture for adjacent edges in independence polynomials
context.statement: Let $\mathsf K_n$ be the complete graph and let $Z(\mathbf I\mathsf K_n;\mathbf y)$ be the partition function of its independent-set system. For edges $e,f$, let $\Delta Z\{e,f\}$ denote the Rayleigh difference. **Adjacent-edge coefficient conjecture.** If $e$ and $f$ are adjacent edges in $\mathsf K_n$, then $\Delta Z(\mathbf I\mathsf K_n)\{e,f\}$ has nonnegative coefficients. The claim has been checked for $n\leq6$ and is open in general.
context.source_name: David G. Wagner, “Negatively correlated random variables and Mason's conjecture”, arXiv:math/0602648 (2006).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602648

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “A positive solution to the Big Conjecture would be a very good thing.”

context.title: Cohomology conjecture for the complete graph \(K_5\)
context.statement:
Let $K_5$ be the complete graph on five vertices. **Complete-graph $K_5$ conjecture.**

$$
H^{1,3m-2}_{{\mathcal A}_m}(K_5)=\begin{cases}\mathbb{Z}_2\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{5},&m=2;\\mathbb{Z}_2\oplus\mathbb{Z}_3^{4}\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{10},&m=3;\\mathbb{Z}_2^{5}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_m^{10}\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{10},&m=4;\\mathbb{Z}_2^{5}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_m^{10}\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{10},&m>4,\ m\text{ odd};\\mathbb{Z}_2^{10}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_m^{10}\oplus\mathbb{Z}^{10},&m>5,\ m\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source presents this as a conjectural computational pattern and gives no resolution.
context.source_name: Milena D. Pabiniak, Jozef H. Przytycki and Radmila Sazdanovic, “On the first group of the chromatic cohomology of graphs”, arXiv:math/0607326 (2006).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607326

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2006). “This is still an open problem, and motivated by this we thought that for $\A_3$ graph homology torsion will be rather limited.”

context.title: Bonnington–Watkins conjecture on infinite face-boundaries
context.statement: Let $G$ be a locally finite vertex-transitive graph of connectivity $3$, and consider a planar embedding of $G$. **Bonnington–Watkins conjecture.** No such embedding has a vertex incident with more than one infinite face-boundary. The conjecture is refuted by examples in this paper, which give 3-connected graphs with no finite face-boundary.
context.source_name: Agelos Georgakopoulos, “The planar cubic Cayley graphs”, arXiv:1102.2087 (2011).
context.references:

context.title: Ternary-partition numerator conjecture at minus one
context.statement:
Let $\mathcal T(n)$ be the set of ternary partitions of $n$, meaning partitions whose parts are powers of $3$, and define 
$$
s(n)=\mathrm{num}_{\mathcal T}(n,-1).
$$
 **Ternary-partition evaluation conjecture.** One has $s(1)=s(2)=1$ and, for every relevant integer $n$, 
$$
s(3n)=s(3n+1)=s(3n+2)=3^{\mathrm{val}_3((3n)!)}.
$$
 This is one of the open questions proposed for restricted partition sets and remains open.
context.source_name: Cristina Ballantine, George Beck, Brooke Feigon and Kathrin Maurischat, “Reciprocals of Subsum Polynomials”, arXiv:2605.10512 (2026).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10512

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026). “In Section , we discuss open questions for sums of reciprocals of subsum polynomials defined on restricted sets of partitions.”

context.title: Unimodality conjecture for the even part of reciprocal subsum numerators
context.statement:
Let $\mathrm{num}(n,x)$ be the numerator polynomial associated with sums of reciprocals of subsum polynomials over partitions of $n$, and write 
$$
\mathrm{num}(n,x)=\mathrm{num}_0(n,x)+\mathrm{num}_1(n,x),
$$
 where $\mathrm{num}_0(n,x)$ is even and $\mathrm{num}_1(n,x)$ is odd. **Unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial $\mathrm{num}_0(n,x)$ is unimodal. The paper reports experimental evidence for this conjecture, which remains open.

context.title: Ternary-partition numerator conjecture at one
context.statement:
Let $\mathcal T(n)$ be the set of ternary partitions of $n$, meaning partitions whose parts are powers of $3$, and define 
$$
t(n)=\mathrm{num}_{\mathcal T}(n,1).
$$
 Let $\Delta$ denote the operator used in the source. **Ternary-partition recurrence conjecture.** One has $t(1)=t(2)=1$, 
$$
t(3n)=t(3n+1)=t(3n+2),
$$
 and 
$$
t(n)=\Delta\bigl(t(3n-2)/2^{2n}\bigr).
$$
 The statement is posed as an open question, but the supplied context does not define $\Delta$, so its precise meaning requires checking the paper.

context.title: Irreducibility conjecture for reciprocal subsum numerators
context.statement: Let $n\geq 1$, and let $\mathrm{num}(n,x)$ denote the numerator polynomial associated with sums of reciprocals of subsum polynomials over partitions of $n$. **Irreducibility conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$, the polynomial $\mathrm{num}(n,x)$ is irreducible over the integers. This is supported by numerical evidence and is posed as an open question.

context.title: Cyclotomic nondivisibility conjecture for binary-partition numerators
context.statement:
Let $\mathcal B(n)$ be the set of binary partitions of $n$, and let $\mathrm{num}_{\mathcal B}(n,x)$ be the associated numerator polynomial. **Binary-partition nondivisibility conjecture.** For every $n\geq 2$ and every integer $i$ satisfying $2^i\leq n$, 
$$
1+x^{2^i}\nmid \mathrm{num}_{\mathcal B}(n,x).
$$
 The paper gives evidence for this conjecture, which remains open.

context.title: Cohomology conjecture for the complete graph \(K_4\)
context.statement:
Let $K_4$ be the complete graph on four vertices. **Complete-graph $K_4$ conjecture.** For every $m\geq4$,

$$
H^{1,2m-1}_{{\mathcal A}_m}(K_4)=\mathbb{Z}_m^4\oplus\mathbb{Z}_2\oplus\mathbb{Z}^2.
$$

The paper reports verification for $m\leq14$, but does not establish the stated range in general.

context.title: Ruzsa's sumset conjecture for finite sets of squares
context.statement:
For a finite set $E$ of squares, write $E+E=\{x+y:x,y\in E\}$. **Ruzsa's conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$,

$$
|E+E|\gg |E|^{2-\epsilon}.
$$

The source states that Chang's conjecture implies this one, while the Bombieri--Lang conjecture yields only weaker bounds; its general validity remains open.

context.title: The logarithmic additive-energy conjecture for subsets of squares
context.statement:
For a set $E\subset\{1^2,\ldots,N^2\}$ of squares, let $r_{E+E}(m)$ count representations of $m$ as a sum of two elements of $E$. **The logarithmic energy conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that

$$
\sum_m r_{E+E}^2(m)\ll |E|^2(\log N)^C.
$$

The source states this as the corresponding conjecture for arbitrary subsets of the first $N$ squares and leaves it open.

context.title: Cohomology conjecture for the square with a diagonal
context.statement:
Let $P_3|P_3$ denote the graph formed by gluing two triangles along an edge, and let $H^{i,j}_{{\mathcal A}_m}(G)$ denote the corresponding graph cohomology. **Square-with-diagonal conjecture.** For $m>2$,

$$
H^{1,2m-1}_{{\mathcal A}_m}(P_3|P_3)=\mathbb{Z}_m^2\oplus\mathbb{Z}.
$$

The paper reports verification for $m\leq 15$, but does not establish the general claim.
